title: Stabilizer-preserving etale maps descend over affine groupoid moduli
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal Z$ an algebraic stack over $k$ admitting a representable surjective finite flat finitely presented map from an affine scheme. Choose its affine finite locally free groupoid presentation and let $f:\mathcal Z\to M$ be its invariant-spectrum morphism [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-groupoid-moduli]. Let $h:\mathcal Z'\to\mathcal Z$ be representable by algebraic spaces, separated, etale, and stabilizer-preserving, meaning $I_{\mathcal Z'}\simeq\mathcal Z'\times_{\mathcal Z}I_{\mathcal Z}$. Then there are a $k$-scheme $M'$, a separated etale map $u:M'\to M$, and a uniform categorical morphism $f':\mathcal Z'\to M'$ for which $f h=u f'$ and $\mathcal Z'\simeq\mathcal Z\times_M M'$ over both factors. The morphism $f'$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and a universal homeomorphism, and induces a bijection on isomorphism classes of $\Omega$-points for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. The descended square is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with $h$ and $f$. Representable separated etale stabilizer-preserving morphisms are stable under composition and base change by algebraic stacks. Algebraic stacks and quasi-coherent sheaves have the meanings in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and algebraic spaces have the meaning in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A 2-fibre product retains the specified isomorphism between the two images of an object. For an affine groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$, the groupoid laws are those of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]; $[U/R]$ denotes the fppf stackification of the groupoid with objects $U(T)$ and arrows $R(T)$ on test schemes $T$. The point space of an algebraic stack consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth surjective scheme atlas. A morphism is a universal homeomorphism if every base change by an algebraic stack induces a homeomorphism of these point spaces. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact inverse images of affine scheme tests, and quasi-separated means quasi-compact relative diagonal, both on scheme charts. A morphism $f:\mathcal Z\to M$ to an algebraic space is uniform categorical if, for every flat algebraic-space map $M'\to M$ and every algebraic space $T/k$, composition with $f_{M'}$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Mor}_k(M',T)$ to $\operatorname{Mor}_k(\mathcal Z\times_M M',T)$. Inertia has the object-with-automorphism description above; separated means proper relative diagonal [def-weil-proper-morphism], and etaleness and flatness are tested on scheme charts [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism].

proof.text: Choose the given finite flat affine cover $U\to\mathcal Z$ and put $V=\mathcal Z'\times_{\mathcal Z}U$. Base change preserves representable etaleness by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] and separatedness by [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence]. Thus $V\to U$ is a separated etale algebraic-space map. Its diagonal is a closed immersion on scheme tests by the representable clause of [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence], so [lem-a1-separated-etale-space-scheme] makes $V$ a scheme etale over $U$. It is locally quasi-finite over $U$ by [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite] (applied to the identity chart of $V$), and separated, so every finite subset of $V$ lies in an affine open by [lem-sfb-separated-lqf-affine-finite-set], as $U$ is affine. The map $V\to\mathcal Z'$ is a finite flat cover by base change of the chosen cover. Thus $Q=V\times_{\mathcal Z'}V$ is a scheme with finite locally free projections, by the definition of a representable finite flat finitely presented map and [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations](2) to obtain $\mathcal Z'=[V/Q]$. The orbit of any point is finite, since it is the image of a finite fibre of $s_Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-groupoid-invariant-affine] to each orbit, obtaining a covering by invariant affine opens $V_i$. The invariant-open correspondence of [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-quotient-open-presentation] gives corresponding open substacks $\mathcal Z_i'=[V_i/Q_i]$, where $Q_i=s_Q^{-1}(V_i)=t_Q^{-1}(V_i)$ is finite locally free over $V_i$, hence finite and affine over the affine $V_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 0DUS, first paragraph, through the invariant affine covering; schemehood and affine neighbourhoods from spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03XU, 03XX and more-morphisms.tex Tag 07S0

proof.text: Write $R=U\times_{\mathcal Z}U$. For $V_i\to U$, the source and target squares of $Q_i\to R$ are cartesian: first $Q\simeq R\times_{s,U}V\simeq R\times_{t,U}V$ by associating the 2-fibre products, and then restrict to the invariant open $V_i$. The stabilizer square is cartesian because its fibres are the automorphisms of the chosen objects, and $h$ identifies their automorphism sheaves. The map $V_i\to U$ is etale. Set $C=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)^R$ and $D_i=\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O)^{Q_i}$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-groupoid-etale-invariant-comparison] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $(a,b)=(V_i\to U,Q_i\to R)$: $N_i=\operatorname{Spec}D_i\to M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale and $V_i\simeq U\times_MN_i$. The source square then gives $Q_i\simeq R\times_MN_i$, respecting all operations. Quotient base change from [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-presentation-calculus] gives $\mathcal Z_i'\simeq\mathcal Z\times_MN_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-groupoid-moduli] to $(V_i,Q_i)$: $q_i:\mathcal Z_i'\to N_i$ is uniform categorical and a universal homeomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DUQ, three cartesian squares and final paragraph; Tag 0DUS, affine quotient charts

proof.text: Let $\mathcal W_{ij}=\mathcal Z_i'\cap\mathcal Z_j'$. Since $|q_i|$ is a homeomorphism, its image is an open subset $N_{ij}\subseteq N_i$, and $\mathcal W_{ij}=\mathcal Z_i'\times_{N_i}N_{ij}$. Indeed on each scheme test both sides are open subschemes with the same point set, so are the same open subscheme. The restricted map to $N_{ij}$ remains uniform categorical: for any flat $T\to N_{ij}$ the composite to $N_i$ is flat (an open immersion identifies local rings, so is flat), so the defining factorization bijection for $q_i$ applies. Construct $N_{ji}$ in the same way. Categorical uniqueness gives mutually inverse maps $\phi_{ij}:N_{ij}\to N_{ji}$ with $\phi_{ij}q_i=q_j$ on $\mathcal W_{ij}$: each composite with its reverse becomes the identity after $q_i$ or $q_j$, hence is the identity. These maps are over $M$ for the same reason.

source.place: Tag 0DUS, overlap isomorphisms; elementary use of uniform categorical factorization

proof.text: On $\mathcal W_{ijk}$ the maps $\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}$ and $\phi_{ik}$ both compose with its restricted quotient map to the same restriction of $q_k$, so categorical uniqueness makes them equal. Moreover $\phi_{ij}^{-1}(N_{ji}\cap N_{jk})=N_{ij}\cap N_{ik}$: pull back to $\mathcal W_{ij}$, where both sides are exactly $\mathcal W_{ijk}$, and use the homeomorphism on point spaces. Also $\phi_{ii}=1$. Thus these are the precise gluing data required by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes]. Glue the $N_i$ to a $k$-scheme $M'$. Their maps to $M$ agree on the overlaps, so glue to $u:M'\to M$; it is etale by source locality in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. On any scheme test $T\to\mathcal Z'$, the inverse images of $\mathcal Z_i'$ form an open cover; the maps to $N_i\subseteq M'$ agree on intersections and glue to $T\to M'$. They are compatible with every test morphism, giving $f':\mathcal Z'\to M'$. Its inverse image of $N_i$ is $\mathcal Z_i'$ by the same open-subscheme point test. The local cartesian squares of step 2 therefore give $\mathcal Z'\simeq\mathcal Z\times_MM'$, with both projections specified.

source.place: Tag 0DUS, omitted cocycle computation and scheme gluing

proof.text: For $q:V\to M'$ the inverse image of $N_i$ is $V_i$ and its restriction is the invariant-ring map $V_i\to N_i$. By [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants] this map is integral. Each restriction is universally closed by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed]. Thus $q$ is universally closed: after any scheme base change, the inverse images of the $N_i$ are open covers, and the image of a closed subset intersects each such open in the closed image under the restricted map. Closedness is local on an open cover. It is surjective: $V\to\mathcal Z'$ is the surjective cover of step 1 and $f'$ is a base change of the universal homeomorphism $f$. Its composite $V\to M$ is separated, since $V\to U$ is separated and $U\to M$ has affine source [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Composition is separated by [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-separated] with base $M$, source $V$, target $M'$ to conclude that $u$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 0DUS, final paragraph; integrality of local atlas maps from Tag 03BJ

proof.text: The morphism $f'$ is the base change of $f$ along $u$. The node [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-groupoid-moduli] supplies quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, the universal homeomorphism property and the geometric-point bijection for $f$. Apply the quasi-compact base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism] both to $f$ and to its relative diagonal; the diagonal of $f'$ is the corresponding base change of the diagonal of $f$. This proves quasi-compactness of $f'$ and of its relative diagonal; the universal homeomorphism assertion pulls back directly from its definition, by associating arbitrary further base changes. For an algebraically closed $\Omega/k$ and $m'\in M'(\Omega)$, objects of the fibre of $f'$ over $m'$ are precisely objects $z\in\mathcal Z(\Omega)$ with $f(z)=u(m')$, since $M$ is a sheaf with no nonidentity automorphisms. The bijection for $f$ gives exactly one isomorphism class. Finally, for a flat $T\to M'$ its composite $T\to M$ is flat, since $u$ is etale and flat and flat maps compose [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Apply the uniform categorical property of $f$ to this composite and use the cartesian identification; this is exactly uniform categoricality of $f'$.

source.place: Tags 0DUP and 0DUR, uniform property after flat base change; consequences of the constructed cartesian square

proof.text: If $(M'',f'',u'')$ is another square with the asserted properties, categoricality of $f'$ factors $f''$ uniquely as $a f'$, and categoricality of $f''$ factors $f'$ uniquely as $b f''$. Thus $ba=1$ and $ab=1$ by precomposition with the respective categorical maps. The equation $u''a=u$ follows by precomposing with $f'$ and using the given compatibility with $h,f$. Any other compatible isomorphism also has composite $f''$ with $f'$ and hence equals $a$. This proves uniqueness of the descended square, including its cartesian identification, which is the comparison with the two specified projections.

source.place: Tag 0DUS, categorical uniqueness of the gluing; elementary universal-property argument

proof.text: Representability by algebraic spaces is stable under composition and arbitrary 2-base change by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], and etaleness by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], and separatedness by [lem-sfb-stack-separation-compactness-permanence]. Stabilizers compose because the induced automorphism-sheaf maps compose. For a base change $\mathcal B\to\mathcal Z$, an object of $\mathcal Z'\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal B$ is $(z',b,\alpha:h(z')\simeq g(b))$. An automorphism is a pair $(a,c)$ satisfying $g(c)\alpha=\alpha h(a)$. Given $c$, the isomorphism on automorphism sheaves for $h$ gives exactly one $a$ with $h(a)=\alpha^{-1}g(c)\alpha$. This construction is natural under every test-scheme pullback. Hence the projection identifies its inertia with the pullback of $I_{\mathcal B}$, proving the stated base-change assertion.
